title: The Manosphere Hits the Mainstream
author: Aaron Renn
summary: The manosphere has evolved from pragmatic relationship advice to a toxic blame culture where women are blamed for society's ills. Modern incels weaponize stigma against any man who discusses sex positively or admits romantic experience. This shift from "understand female preferences and improve yourself" to "women are inherently terrible" represents an incel takeover of masculine online discourse. The new manosphere spreads bleakness about human connection, treating intimacy as a rigged auction rather than a mundane, achievable aspect of life.
points: Old manosphere: pragmatic self-improvement (exercise, fashion, cologne) within realistic female preferences
New manosphere: hostile blame of women for all societal ills; every woman is "mid" at best
Incel influence: weaponizing stigma against men who discuss positive sexual experience or relationships
Cultural shift from "you can improve" to "the system is rigged and hopeless"
Freddie deBoer notes: culture now treats sex/romance as pathological rather than mundane human experience
quotes: I am a more-or-less heterosexual man who has had sex with a non-zero number of woman now provokes a kind of resentful reaction that I find annoying, strange, and honestly kind of anti-human.

The incel's veto is the specific prohibition against men ever frankly discussing sex in any positive way that directly reflects the fact that they have sexual experience and thus have earned the consent of women.

A relative handful of alienated, internet-addled men, marinating in grievance and pseudo-Darwinian fatalism, have managed to inject into the bloodstream of our culture a bleak, hyper-strategized, market-based understanding of intimacy that treats human connection as a ruthless auction.
